name: Mser
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: Le m̀sə̀r compte 33 consonnes auxquelles s'ajoute une nasale syllabique attestée uniquement à l'initiale. [...] Le système vocalique présente phonétiquement 6 voyelles brèves (i, e, a, o, u ə), qu'il n'est pas très difficile de réduire à 2 (a, ə) structurellement. Le système tonal compte deux registres (Haut et Bas) comme toutes les autres langues « kotoko ». Des tons modulés peuvent occasionnellement se rencontrer, sur des emprunts, par exemple.
new_statements.translation: Mser has 33 consonants, to which is added a syllabic nasal attested only word-initially. [...] The vowel system phonetically shows 6 short vowels (i, e, a, o, u, ə), which it is not very hard to reduce to 2 (a, ə) structurally. The tone system has two registers (High and Low), like all the other 'Kotoko' languages. Contour tones can occasionally be met, on loanwords for example.
new_statements.citation: Tourneux, Henry. 2019. Le syntagme nominal dans le parler « kotoko » de Kousseri. In H. Tourneux & Y. Treis (eds), Topics in Chadic Linguistics X (BICCL 9, Villejuif 2017), 241-257. Cologne: Rüdiger Köppe. HAL halshs-03226997.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Mser is described as a two-register (H/L) tone language, like the rest of Kotoko; the only published description of the language says nothing about word stress or accent at all. Tone is lexically and grammatically active (feminine derivation bə̀skwàn 'horse' / bə̀skwán 'mare'; tone-pattern change is one of the plural-formation devices; the relative marker rí raises the tone of the following noun, preprint p. 8). No stress placement rule can be extracted.
new_statements.exceptions: Contour (modulated) tones occur occasionally, e.g. on loanwords; otherwise only level H and L.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about the lexical tone system of the word (nouns in citation and in noun-phrase context); the paper is a noun-phrase study with a one-page phonological sketch, transcriptions are largely surface-phonetic (note 1). Word stress is not discussed in any domain.
new_statements.identity_note: Tourneux 2019 describes the « kotoko » speech of the town of Kousseri, autonym [m̀sə̀r], which is exactly Glottolog's Mser (mser1242, ISO kqx; alt. names Kuseri/Kousseri/Msir/Klesem). Tourneux places it with Lagwan, Houlouf and Kala-Kafra in 'Kotoko central' (Gravina 2014: Kotoko Centre = Lagwan + Mser). Data are from Kousseri-town speakers recorded in 2000 (informants born 1928-1960); Ethnologue's other dialect names (Gawi, Houlouf, Kabe, Kalo) are not covered. The language is moribund (Campbell et al. 2022 via Glottolog).

sources.note: Section 'Phonologie' (preprint p. 5, PDF p. 6): 33 consonants plus an initial syllabic nasal, 6 phonetic short vowels reducible to /a, ə/; 'Le système tonal compte deux registres (Haut et Bas) comme toutes les autres langues « kotoko ». Des tons modulés peuvent occasionnellement se rencontrer, sur des emprunts, par exemple.' Nothing on stress or accent anywhere in the paper; tone changes are used in feminine derivation and plural formation (p. 5-6). Data from a 2000 LLACAN field mission at Kousseri (three informants).
